statement: For used cars of one model, the line of fit $\hat{y} = 24{,}000 - 1{,}800x$ predicts the selling price $\hat{y}$, in dollars, from the age $x$ of the car in years. A $6$-year-old car of this model sold for $\$14{,}500$. The residual for a data point is the actual value minus the predicted value. What is the residual, in dollars, for this car?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the actual price from the predicted price, but a residual is actual minus predicted, so my sign is backwards.
I subtracted the sale price from 24,000 and never used the age of the car to find the predicted price.
I found the predicted price of 13,200 dollars and stopped there instead of comparing it with the actual price.

hints: First find what the line predicts for a $6$-year-old car.
The predicted price is $24{,}000 - 1{,}800(6)$. Then subtract that from the actual price.
The prediction is $\$13{,}200$, so the residual is $14{,}500 - 13{,}200$.

solutions.reliable: The predicted price is $24{,}000 - 1{,}800(6) = 24{,}000 - 10{,}800 = 13{,}200$ dollars. The residual is actual minus predicted: $14{,}500 - 13{,}200 = 1{,}300$ dollars. The positive residual means the car sold for more than the line predicts.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
